issues.title: Stated sampling procedure runs the flow in the wrong direction

and that $\|u^\mu\|_{C^1}$ can be bounded by a constant $c_{d,\kappa,\mathcal{K}}$ by~\cite[Theorem 4.12]{marzouk2025} depending only on $d,\kappa,\mathcal{K}$.
there exist a constants $\tilde{c}_{d,k,\kappa,\mathcal{K}}$ depending on $d,k,\kappa,\mathcal{K}$, such that if we choose a neural network architecture

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption \ref{main_assumptions} controls only the values of the target densities ($\kappa\le f_\mu\le\mathcal K$) and their membership in $C^k$; it imposes no uniform bound on $\|f_\mu\|_{C^k}$ over $\mathcal T$. The displacement field inherits the derivatives of $f_\mu$: for $d=1$, $T=F_\mu^{-1}\circ F_\nu$ satisfies $T''=-f_\mu'(T)T'/f_\mu(T)^2$, which is unbounded on $\mathcal T$ (take $f_\mu=c+a\sin(Mx)$ with $0<a<c$, which stays in $[\kappa,\mathcal K]$ while $\|f_\mu\|_{C^k}\sim aM^k$). Hence $\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal T}\|u^\mu\odiv\eta_d\|_{C^k}$ and $\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal T}\|u^\mu\|_{C^1}$ are infinite, so the uniform constants the proof relies on do not exist as stated and the best-approximation bound \eqref{c1_target_approx_thm} and model-error bound \eqref{kl_target_approx_thm} cannot hold uniformly over $\mathcal T$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a uniform smoothness bound to the target class, e.g. require $\|f_\mu\|_{C^k([0,1]^d)}\le M$ for all $\mu\in\mathcal T$ (a bounded Hölder ball), and let all constants depend on $M$ as well; the proof structure, the rate $K^{-(k-1)}$ and the PAC conclusion then hold for that class.
issues.overall_effect: The $\mu$-uniform model-error bound is unreliable, so the main PAC theorem, which quantifies over all $\mu\in\mathcal T$ with $\mu$-independent constants and thresholds, becomes unreliable as well; distributions in $\mathcal T$ with large $C^k$ norms lose the advertised guarantee.
issues.title: Uniform model-error bounds use target-class regularity that the assumptions do not provide
issues.why_classification: Inserting the missing boundedness hypothesis is a short local change that preserves the method, the rates and the PAC form of the conclusion, but it necessarily narrows the quantified target class (uniformity over all $C^k$ densities bounded away from zero is lost), so the repair exceeds a purely minor one while avoiding any new proof architecture.

it is possible to choose a threshold $m(n)$ for the number of quadrature points (i.e., a sparsity level $\ell(n)$ large enough) such that

issues.failure_explanation: The quadrature target \eqref{eq:main_thm_sg_error_bd} contains the factor $1+\sqrt d\exp(\sqrt d\sqrt q\,\operatorname{Lip}_1^\Theta(L_n,W_n))$ with $q\le L_n(W_n+1)W_n$ and $L_n,W_n\to\infty$; hence the admissible node count $m(n)$ tends to infinity with $n$. Choosing $m(\varepsilon,\delta)=m(n(\varepsilon,\delta))$ therefore does not make \eqref{eq:main_thm_sg_error_bd} hold for any $n>n(\varepsilon,\delta)$, and the final quantifier step is invalid. The argument establishes only the diagonal statement 'for every $n$ there is $m(n,\varepsilon,\delta)$', while the statement and definition \eqref{defn:pac_learnability} demand thresholds that work for all larger $n$ and $m$. For fixed $m$ no such uniform bound is available, since admissible learned maps in the growing classes $\mathcal H_2^{L_n,W_n}$ may oscillate ever faster, making $\qoi\circ\Phi^{\hat\theta_n}$ arbitrarily hard for a fixed sparse grid.

failure_location.quote: and a threshold $m(\varepsilon, \delta) := m(n(\varepsilon, \delta))$ on the number of quadrature points such that \eqref{eq:main_thm_sg_error_bd} holds, for all $n \geq n(\varepsilon,\delta)$ and all $m \geq m(\varepsilon,\delta)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the guarantee with a quadrature threshold allowed to depend on the sample size: for every $\varepsilon,\delta>0$ there are $n(\varepsilon,\delta)$ and a map $n\mapsto m(n,\varepsilon,\delta)$ such that $\mathbb{P}(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{total}}>\varepsilon)\le\delta$ for all $n\ge n(\varepsilon,\delta)$ and $m\ge m(n,\varepsilon,\delta)$, and adjust \eqref{defn:pac_learnability} accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: PAC-learnability in the sense of \eqref{defn:pac_learnability} (fixed sample-size and sparsity thresholds valid for all larger $n,\ell$) is not established; only a joint/diagonal version in which the quadrature budget grows with the sample size follows, and the abstract's PAC claim inherits this weakening.
issues.title: PAC guarantee needs a quadrature budget growing with the sample size
issues.why_classification: The proof already delivers the diagonal version, so a limited weakening of the threshold quantifiers preserves the method, the rates and the advertised asymptotic consistency; but the fixed-threshold PAC statement of \eqref{defn:pac_learnability} is lost and the required quadrature budget grows with $n$, which exceeds a minor local repair without forcing a new proof architecture or abandoning the result.
